div.head: II Atr 9.3
div.ab: Gif he ðonne ðære freonda hæfð, ðe þæt don durron, ðonne berst se team, swa wel swa he liues wære ⁊ sylf andsæc worhte; stent ðonne ðeofscyldig se ðe hit on handa hæfð: forðam a bið andsæc swiðere ðonne onsagu.

Si tunc amicos habeat, qui audeant hoc facere, tunc deficit aduocatio, sicut si ille uiueret ac negaret; et habeatur furti reus ille qui in manus habet: quia semper est negatio fortior quam affirmatio.

Gif he ðonne ðære freonda hæfð ðe þæt don durron, ðonne berst se team, swa wel swa he liues wære ⁊ sylf andsæc worhte; stent ðonne ðeofscyldig se ðe hit on handa hæfð, forðam a bið andsæc swiðere ðonne onsagu.

Wenn nämlich der [Verstorbene] solche Freunde besitzt, die das zu thun wagen, dann bricht der Gewährzug so gut, als wäre er am Leben und vollzöge selbst diese Leugnung. Dann steht Diebstahls schuldig, wer das [im Anefang Eingeklagte] in Besitz hat: denn immer ist Ableugnung [des Verklagten] näher zum Beweise als Klage.

For if the [dead man] has such friends as dare do that, then the vouching to warranty fails, just as if he were alive and made the denial himself. Then whoever has [the attached item] in his possession stands guilty of theft: for denial is always stronger than accusation.

If, however, he has friends who are prepared to do so, the vouching to warranty shall fail as completely as if he had himself been alive and had proved his denial. Then he, in whose possession the goods are, will be held guilty of theft, because denial is always stronger than accusation.

note.seg: Über den Gen. s. o. II 108 Sp. 1 letzte Z.; Toller 497
On the gen. see above II 108 col. 1 last l.; Toller 497
Vgl. Gl Anefang 17b. 23 (wo man das Zitat dieser Stelle 4 Z. höher rücke)
Cf. Gl Anefang 17b. 23 (where the citation of this passage should be moved 4 ll. higher)

Nicht ‘als Dieb’; der falsche Gewähr Ziehende zahlt mindestens dem Anefänger Busse, dem Nachmanne Ersatz, dem Gerichtsherrn Strafgeld des Diebstahls (II Cn 24, 1) oder sogar Wergeld (Leis Wl 21, 2), oder es geht ihm wie dem falschen Anrufer von Kaufzeugen laut IV Eg 11¹·² ans Leben. Im letzteren Falle würde der falschen Gewährzuges Überführte als ertappter Handhafter (s. d. Gl 5d) behandelt

Not ‘as a thief’; the man who falsely vouches to warranty pays at the least compensation to the attacher, restitution to the subsequent possessor, and the fine for theft to the lord of the court (II Cn 24, 1), or even wergild (Leis Wl 21, 2), or else, like the man who falsely calls on witnesses of purchase according to IV Eg 11¹·², he forfeits his life. In the latter case the man convicted of false vouching to warranty would be treated as one caught in the act (see that word in Gl 5d)
Die Beweisnähe (s. d. Gl 2. a) geniesst der bezogene Tote, nicht etwa der ursprünglich im Anefang beklagte Besitzer.—Vgl. Gl Sprichwort 1
The right to proof (see that word in Gl 2. a) is enjoyed by the dead man vouched, not, say, by the possessor originally accused in the attachment. — Cf. Gl Sprichwort 1
For other instances of habban with a partitive genitive see In. 32; 66; Af. 42, 1 and 3.
In view of IV Edg. 11 the culprit might be in danger of losing his life.
